title: Supported finite-stage local systems do not detect the coefficient-topology scalar-unit defect
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended $\ell$-adic norm topology. On profinite sets with finite jointly surjective covers let
$$C(S)=\{f\in C(S,\Omega):f(S)\subset E\text{ for some finite }\mathbf Q_\ell\subset E\subset\Omega\},\qquad B(S)=C(S,\Omega).$$
These are the coefficient rings of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Put $C_T=p_T^*C$, $B_T=p_T^*B$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and let $c_T:C_T\to B_T$ be induced by inclusion. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $J_X=B_X\otimes^L_{C_X}-$ and $U_X=\operatorname{Res}_{c_X}$, and let $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to U_XJ_X$ be their derived adjunction unit [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars], represented on a K-flat resolution by $v\mapsto1\otimes v$.

Choose two constructible locally closed immersions $a:S\hookrightarrow X$, $b:T\hookrightarrow X$ [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Define $a_!=i_*j_!$ after factoring $a=i\circ j$ into an open immersion into its closure followed by the closed immersion, and likewise for $b$, using the exact coefficient-module functors of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement]. Choose finite intermediate fields $E,F\subset\Omega$, and lisse modules $L$ over $A_{E,S}=p_S^*C(-,E)$ and $M$ over $A_{F,T}=p_T^*C(-,F)$ [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module], with the restricted norm topologies [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Set
$$G=a_!\bigl(C_S\otimes^L_{A_{E,S}}L[0]\bigr),\qquad H=b_!\bigl(C_T\otimes^L_{A_{F,T}}M[0]\bigr).$$
For every distinguished triangle $H\xrightarrow{\eta_H}U_XJ_XH\to Q_H\to H[1]$ [def-weil-triangulated-category] and every integer $n$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_X})}(G,Q_H[n])=0.$$
Both supports, both finite fields and both local systems vary independently. Empty supports and rank-zero local systems are included. This is a statement only about these two finite-stage supported local systems and the specified scalar unit; it imposes no flatness on $c_X$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-supported-common-field-scalar-models] to the independently chosen supports, fields and lisse modules. It gives $E_0=EF$, $A=A_{E_0,X}$ and bounded constructible $K,N$ with normalized natural identifications $G\simeq S_CK$, $H\simeq S_CN$, $J_XG\simeq S_BK$, $J_XH\simeq S_BN$. Here $S_R(V)=R_X\otimes_A^L V$. These identifications preserve the specified scalar units, so they also identify scalar extension on morphisms.

Apply [lem-sfb-finite-model-topology-derived-hom] to the bounded constructible common-field models. Its final globalHomComparison is the globalization of the actual scalar Hom comparison followed by reassociation on both Hom inputs. Naturality of restrictionSections moves that final isomorphism outside globalization, where it cancels. Thus the globalized scalar Hom comparison itself is invertible.

source.place: Paragraph (3); derived Hom comparison, returned steps 5–6.

proof.text: Compose the scalar adjunction with the two tensor-Hom adjunctions. Uniqueness of right adjoints gives an isomorphism between restricted target internal Hom and source internal Hom after restriction. The five defining Hom bijections show that the restriction mate of the scalar-extended evaluation, followed by this isomorphism, equals internal Hom applied to the actual scalar unit: the scalar tensorator and its inverse cancel, leaving naturality of the unit and the tensor-Hom counit identity. Applying sections preserves that isomorphism. The invertibility from step 2 therefore makes global internal Hom of the actual unit invertible. Apply [lem-sfb-global-internal-hom-detection] in each degree and transport the result through the isomorphisms of step 1 by naturality of the unit.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent topology-comparison argument; adjunction transfers the comparison to the specified unit.

proof.text: Let the triangle in the assertion be arbitrary and let $q:G\to Q_H[n]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] applied also to the shifted and rotated distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category], its boundary $dq:G\to H[n+1]$ is killed by $\eta_H[n+1]$. Step 3 makes that map on Hom injective, so $dq=0$. Exactness at $Q_H[n]$ gives $q=vh$ for some $h:G\to U_XJ_XH[n]$. Surjectivity in step 3 writes $h=\eta_H[n]u$; consecutive triangle arrows compose to zero, so $q=v\eta_H[n]u=0$. Thus every element of the asserted Hom group is zero. Nothing depended on a chosen cone, a nonempty support, a positive rank, or a relation between $S,T$ or $E,F$, so the asserted edge cases are included.
